## Source: amazon-inspector (ac5f1e73e5038ae7d26af2daaf68855c65aa60f1e0e25da5b0b4827332d6037c)
The sdist's setup.py executes a pingback routine at install time that collects installer identity and host details via subprocess calls to whoami, id, hostname, and cat /etc/hosts, together with the current working directory and a timestamp, and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded URL https://pingback.zsdsh.xyz/depconf/demo-pingtest-xyz/. The behavior runs automatically when the sdist is built on install (the package ships no wheel, so a default pip install builds the sdist on Linux glibc/musl, macOS arm64/x86_64, and Windows x86_64). The /depconf/ path and the package naming are consistent with a dependency-confusion reconnaissance beacon designed to identify internal build hosts that resolve this name from the public index.

## Source: kam193 (d2ce56d3cbce6034dcebd88520ffec19a094c0888b7e797f66c46bc69e8d2eac)
Installing the package or importing the module exfiltrates basic information about the host, and the package has no other purpose.

Category: PROBABLY_PENTEST - Packages looking like typical pentest packages, but also anything that looks like testing, exploring pre-prepared kits, research & co, with clearly low-harm possibilities.


Campaign: GENERIC-standard-pypi-install-pentest


Reasons (based on the campaign):


 - The package contains code to exfiltrate basic data from the system, like IP or username. It has a limited risk.


 - The package overrides the install command in setup.py to execute malicious code during installation.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (6a6aaba095baebff3c4b93c01f23c6a4a41a25f0dd1f9d542a2a7455518ae9b7)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'demo-pingtest-xyz' @ 0.0.1 (pypi) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package executes one or more commands associated with malicious behavior.
